newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hollywood stars blast Germany over Scientologists.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood stars blast Germany over Scientologists.

text.p: A group of 26 American celebrities published an "open letter" to Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Thursday accusing Germany of persecution of Scientologists.
Signed by Dustin Hoffman, Goldie Hawn, Oliver Stone, Mario Puzo and Gore Vidal, the letter was printed as a full-page advertisement in the Paris-based International Herald Tribune.
It called on Kohl to bring "an end to this shameful pattern of organised persecution" which it compared with Nazi Germany's treatment of Jews in the 1930s.

The letter writers said they were not members of the Church of Scientology but were deeply concerned that Germany, and Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in particular, had organised boycotts of entertainers such as Tom Cruise, John Travolta and Chick Corea because of their religious beliefs.

"In the Germany of the 1930s, Hitler made religious intolerance official government policy," the letter stated. "Jews were first marginalised, then excluded from many activities, then vilified and ultimately subjected to unspeakable horrors."
It added: "In the 1930s, it was the Jews. Today it is the Scientologists."

The letter compared the Nazi book burnings of the 1930s to the boycott last summer called by the CDU's youth wing against the 1996 Tom Cruise film "Mission Impossible" because Cruise is a well-known Scientologist.

"These acts are intolerable in any country that conceives of itself as a modern democracy," the letter said. "This organised oppression is beginning to sound familiar...like the Germany of 1936 rather than 1996. It should be stopped -- now, before it spreads and increases in virulence as it did before."
A spokesman for the International Herald Tribune said the typical cost of a full-page ad was $61,000.
